widgets.name: About
widgets.text:
Docket No. TTB-2026-0005, Notice No. 243 (91 FR 52576). Prepared by Dan McLaughlin, Robert Clay Vineyards (petitioner).
dan@robertclayvineyards.com, 512.633.8086. License: CC0 1.0 (full text in item 0, the read me) - no attribution required. (TTB's notice, included in folder 2, is a U.S. Government work.)

What the proposed revision changes in Notice No. 243

Steps (10)-(11) and (90)-(100) near Grit use the petition's own wording (as amended June 6, 2023), lane wording included, in place of TTB's steps (10)-(11) and (90)-(92). Within them:

  • steps (93)-(96) are new: they go around a lobe of granite northwest of the area near Grit by a windmill, a fence line and Topaz Lane, instead of the petition's straight line from the marked 1737 to the marked 1762;
  • two flagged changes to the petition's wording: step (90) names the unnamed, intermittent tributary that the petition's line follows from Honey Creek to the marked 1727, and steps (90)-(91) name the roads as Notice No. 243 names them (below).

Away from the area near Grit, two flagged corrections to Notice No. 243's own wording, one word each; the line does not change:

  • step (85) says "the marked 1,802-foot summit", as the Turtle Creek map prints the summit (x1802), where Notice No. 243 says "the marked 1,801-foot summit" (a substantive correction);
  • step (49) says "the marked 1,586-foot elevation point", where Notice No. 243 says "the marked 1,586-elevation point", the only elevation in its steps written without "-foot" (an editorial correction).

TTB's steps (93)-(96) are unchanged, renumbered (101)-(104). Every other step is TTB's published text word for word.

The petition-worded steps are written in TTB's style, as in its published text: "US Highway" (petition "U.S. Highway"), "northeasterly"/"northwesterly" (petition "north-easterly"/"north-westerly"), elevations with a comma ("1,727-foot"; petition "1727-foot") and "then" without a comma, in steps (10), (11), (90)-(92) and (99).

Roads are named as TTB names them: State Highway 29 northwest of the junction near Grit, US Highway 377 on the road the two share from the junction to Mason. The marked 1,727 is on the shared road, so step (90) says US Highway 377 where the petition said State Highway 29, and in step (91) the two names change places: along US Highway 377 to its intersection with State Highway 29 (the petition: along State Highway 29 to its intersection with U.S. Highway 377). The line does not change.

How the line is drawn

Every point is a mark printed on the USGS maps, or a trace of the map's own linework (roads, streams, contours), located on the scanned 1:24,000 sheets; no line comes from another boundary layer.

Lane wording: along the whole highway stretch (steps (10)-(11) and (91)-(92)) the westbound-lane line is drawn 30 m northeast of the highway's center line and the eastbound-lane line 30 m southwest of it, so the boundary is visible beside the road on the maps (the road symbol is about 13 m wide). This is a drawing convention discussed with TTB; the text is unchanged. Honey Creek (step 9) and the tributary (step 90) end where they meet their lane line.

The map

Red: the proposed revision, 193.83 square miles. Blue: the AVA Map Explorer polygon for Notice No. 243, from TTB's live AVAs_Production layer. The Map Explorer polygon was digitized by hand and the proposed revision follows the printed linework, so the two differ a little almost everywhere (median 11 m apart, measured every 2 m along each line). Shaded: every piece of land between them (red: in the proposed revision only; blue: in the Map Explorer polygon only; grey: the proposed text change near Grit); from the same text drawn differently they add up to 682 acres in the proposed revision only and 368 in the Map Explorer polygon only. Ringed: the 6 big differences, where the lines are 100 m or more apart (orange: the two lines take different paths; grey dashed: the proposed text change near Grit). Under them: the USGS geologic units (Town Mountain Granite, younger granitic intrusions, Hickory Sandstone Member formation), shifted about 400 m to sit on the outcrops, and the 13 USGS quadrangles. In the map's layer list, TTB's AVA Map Explorer basemaps holds the Map Explorer's four basemaps (Topographic, Streets, Imagery, USA Topo Maps): turn it on and pick one.

widgets.name: The change near Grit
widgets.text:
Near Grit the proposed text puts back the petition's wording in place of Notice No. 243's steps (10)-(11) and (90)-(92), and adds steps (93)-(96) around a lobe of granite. Turn on The change near Grit in the map's layer list (on by default) to see each line and area.

Of the 15 steps worded differently from Notice No. 243 (Steps reworded, at the top), 13 are here, near Grit: (10)-(11), (90)-(100). The other two, (49) and (85), correct Notice No. 243's own wording elsewhere, one word each; the line does not change. Every other step is Notice No. 243's text word for word.

The lines

  • Put back: the petition's wording, (10)-(11), (90)-(92), (97)-(100)
  • New: (93)-(96), around the granite lobe
  • Replaced: the petition's straight line from the marked 1,737 to the marked 1,762
